Fair challenge, but I'd push back a little. Cannibalization is the one thing that could break my recommendation, so I'll grant it belongs in the structure — but I'd fold it under price rather than make it a separate branch, because the fix is the same either way. If some Starter signups would have paid $100, the answer is still to close the gap: raise Starter toward $55-60 and widen the feature gap so Pro-ready buyers self-select up.

What's strictly missing from my three buckets is the mix question — of the tripling in new customers, how many are net new versus downgrades or deflected Pro prospects. And arguably the shutdown counterfactual: if we kill Starter, do those customers buy Pro or just disappear.

Do we have the Pro new-customer count by month, before and after January 2025? That would show cannibalization directly.
said: Got it. The mix and shutdown counterfactual are now on the table. On what you asked about earlier: The cost to acquire one new customer is $1,200 for Pro, through a sales demo, and $300 for Starter, which is self-serve, and it does not change with volume. Of the 1,050 Pro customers who signed up in January–March 2025, 98.0% were still on Pro after month 1, 94.1% after month 3, 88.6% after month 6 and 78.5% after month 12, so 2.0%, 5.9%, 11.4% and 21.5% had cancelled by those months. Here's an exhibit: Quillpath — New customers per month, by plan (average per month). Let's hold monthly cancellation rates for a little later. What does it tell you about cannibalization, and what does it change in your approach?

grade.note: Closed after both wrap-up probes were spent.

candidateText:
Sure. That's the value of one Starter signup under finance's convention: Starter LTV plus one Pro LTV for each customer who upgrades.

Starter LTV: 40% are still on Starter at month 12, and cancellation is steady month to month, so monthly survival is 0.40^(1/12) ≈ 0.926 — about 7.4% leaving Starter each month, counting cancels and upgrades together. Monthly gross margin is $40 − $10 = $30. So $30 / 0.074 ≈ $405.

Pro LTV: 78.5% still on Pro at month 12, so 0.785^(1/12) ≈ 0.980, about 2.0% monthly churn. Margin $100 − $20 = $80. So $80 / 0.020 = $4,000.

Upgrade stream: 20% of Starter signups upgrade by month 12 and very few after, so 0.20 × $4,000 = $800.

$405 + $800 = $1,205, against $300 CAC — about 4x, clearing the 3x bar.
said: That covers what I wanted to get to. Thanks for working through the case — your written report will follow.
